title: Walter Benjamin in German, 1911–1940: Über den Begriff der Geschichte, Ursprung des deutschen Trauerspiels, the Baudelaire studies, Einbahnstraße, Zur Kritik der Gewalt, Die Aufgabe des Übersetzers with the Tableaux Parisiens, Deutsche Menschen, Das Kunstwerk im Zeitalter seiner technischen Reproduzierbarkeit (third version), Das Leben der Studenten, and ten pieces from periodicals, seven of them from Berliner Kindheit um neunzehnhundert
edition: German Wikisource transcriptions at pinned revisions (thirteen pieces); Internet Archive scans of Deutsche Menschen (1936), the Tableaux Parisiens (1923) and Archiv für Sozialwissenschaft und Sozialpolitik 47 (1920/21); Gesammelte Schriften I–VII, ed. Rolf Tiedemann and Hermann Schweppenhäuser with others (Frankfurt am Main: Suhrkamp), Internet Archive text layers cut to Benjamin's text. Each work's source is named in works.list.
language: deu (the Tableaux Parisiens volume also carries Baudelaire's French)

license.payload: Walter Benjamin died on 26 September 1940; his writings are in the public domain where the term is the author's life plus seventy years. Fourteen of the sixteen items were first printed between 1911 and 1936. The third version of the Kunstwerk essay was first printed after his death; it is held here as German Wikisource transcribes it from Gesammelte Schriften I.2 (Suhrkamp, 1980), text only, with the editors' additions marked there in square brackets. German Wikisource transcriptions are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0. The Internet Archive items for Deutsche Menschen and the Tableaux Parisiens carry the Public Domain Mark 1.0; the Archiv volume carries no mark and was printed in 1920/1921. Each original is held as fetched.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only. Text layers derived from German Wikisource pages carry that source's CC BY-SA 4.0.

pinned_originals.what: The seven volumes of Gesammelte Schriften as open uploads on the Internet Archive (uploaded 2011), text layers. They carry the editors' reports and notes, which are in copyright (Suhrkamp Verlag; Rolf Tiedemann, Hermann Schweppenhäuser and the other editors). They are fixed here by address, size and SHA-256 as fetched, and are not copied into this seat. Each cut in this seat names its volume and its character offsets, so a cut can be checked against the whole.

notes: Text layers from Wikisource are the rendered page with the header box, images and edit links removed; page breaks of the printed source are kept as [S. n] and footnote calls as [n], with the notes at the end. Each layer was checked against its page by character count.
The three Internet Archive layers are uncorrected OCR and are marked so. They are seated so the words can be found; they are not reading texts.

Not seated here, with the reason: 'Die Waffen von morgen' (Vossische Zeitung, 29 June 1925), which the Wikisource author page lists and whose own page attributes to Dora Sophie Benjamin (died 1964). Volume I of the Gesammelte Schriften is cut into eight text layers of Benjamin's words (the theses on history, the Baudelaire studies, Zentralpark, the Trauerspiel book, the Wahlverwandtschaften essay, the dissertation, the Kunstwerk essay's first and third versions, and the appendix). Volumes II to VII are each one cut of Benjamin's text, from the first work to the start of the editors' section; volume V leaves out the editor's introduction at the front, and volume VII stops before the editors' bibliography. Part-title and contents pages that fall inside a cut are left in. Left out of the cuts, each marked in place with its volume offsets (Lee Sharks, 2026-11-28 00:54: 'yup lets cut the non-commons bits'): five pieces signed jointly with a co-author not seventy years dead ('Neapel' with Asja Lacis, died 1979; 'Gehaltserhöhung?! Wo denken Sie hin!' with Wolf Zucker, died 1983; 'Revue oder Theater' with Bernhard Reich, died 1972; 'Vom Weltbürger zum Großbürger' with Willy Haas, died 1973, all in volume IV; 'Das kalte Herz' with Ernst Schoen, died 1960, in volume VII); 'Allemands de quatre-vingt-neuf', which volume IV prints in Marcel Stora's French; and the two records of the January 1928 hashish experiment headed as Ernst Bloch's (died 1977) in volume VI. Kept, as other hands long dead: the protocols written by Ernst Joël (died 1929) and Fritz Fränkel (died 1944); in the Miszellen of volume IV, two poems by Gertrud Kolmar (died 1943), Benjamin's German of Antoine Wiertz (died 1865), and the 'Phantasiesätze' of an unnamed eleven-year-old printed in 1926; and the Passagen-Werk's excerpts from other authors, which are quotation inside Benjamin's own work. Death years were checked on 2026-11-28 against German Wikipedia and, for Joël and Schoen, the Deutsches Literaturarchiv Marbach authority records; Kolmar's and Wiertz's are from memory. The last part of volume IV was read heading by heading for other hands; volumes II, III, V, VI and VII were searched by co-author name only. Cutting volumes II to VII work by work, as volume I is, is owed.
